newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduras public workers launch strike.
newsitem.headline: Honduras public workers launch strike.

text.p: Tens of thousands of government workers in Honduras launched a strike on Friday to demand higher wages, seizing control of several government buildings and bringing most official activity to a halt.

Up to 23,000 public workers took part in the strike, seizing control of dozens of state buildings and blocking the entrances. Workers placed padlocks on the buildings' doors and put up posters that outlined their demands.
Shortly afterwards, dozens of riot police arrived and stood near the striking workers.

"We have decided to occupy the buildings indefinitely due to the government's refusal to negotiate our demands," Manuel Jimenez, the vice-president of the ANDEPH public workers' union, told reporters.
"The government needs to negotiate and not simply tell us that there is not one cent more for public workers," he added.
Government officials warned the workers they would be forcibly removed from the buildings and fired from their jobs if they did not call off the strike within three days.

"Some government ministries have been seized by the strikers. If they cause anarchy, the government will need to take measures to ensure order as directed by the Constitution," said Amilcar Zuniga, head of the government's civil service department.
Col. Julio Chavez, chief of Honduras' police, added: "We are the guarantors of public order and we will dislodge the protesters if they persist in blocking government buildings."
This is the first major public workers' strike faced by the government of President Carlos Roberto Reina, who took power in 1994 and leaves this year after general elections.
Honduras is one of Latin America's poorest countries.

The strike comes following a government move to raise spending on public workers' salaries by $21.6 million (276 million lempiras) -- an increase that fell short of their demands for an increase of $70.5 million (900 million lempiras) on public salaries.
The under-secretary at the Labour Ministry, Felipe Elvir, called on workers to abandon the buildings and said the government would talk with the strikers.
